This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Petitioner is seeking anticipatory bail in connection with a case registered in Crime No.75/2023 of Sanjay Nagar Police Station for offences punishable under Sections 14(c) of the Foreigners Act, 1946 and Sections 114, 465, 468, 471, 420 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State and perused the material on record.
3.
The above mentioned case is registered against accused No.1 on a complaint lodged by the Immigration Officer, Office of the F.R.R.O, Bureau of Immigration, Bengaluru.

4. It is alleged in the complaint that accused No.1 is involved in VISA fraud and cheating the foreign students by providing fraudulent admissions to 104 foreign students at one Savitha Maharshi Degree College located at No.6, 5th Main, NGEF Colony, Sanjaynagar, Bengaluru.
The trust, which runs NC: 2023:KHC:21474 the college has confirmed that no foreign students are enrolled in the said college.

It is further stated that as per immigration records of last one year, there are about 104 foreign students, majority of whom are Yemenese and from among these 104 students, none of them have taken admission in the college but were provided bonafide certificates from the college to obtain services from the F.R.R.O. Bengaluru and all these certificates contained the signature of accused No.1.
5.

The complaint would further reveal that accused No.1 namely, one Sameer Khan claiming himself to be the owner of the college, even though not holding any designation in the administration of the College, issued bogus certificates to the students, as if they are issued by the college to obtain services from FRRO, Bengaluru.
6. Accused No.1 was arrested on 12.04.2023.
It appears that the said accused, in his voluntary statement has stated that he had given the empty letterhead and round seal of the college to the petitioner.

sentences.text: 2 7. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that only on the basis of voluntary statement of accused No.1, the respondent - police have implicated the petitioner as an accused in this case.

He has drawn the attention of the Court to the statement of one Lakshiminarayan (CW.9)
wherein, he has stated it was accused No.1, who had visited his printing press and got printed the letterheads and round seal of the college.
8. Learned HCGP contends that the petitioner is a partner of accused No.1 and he is also involved in the offence.
He submits that the petitioner is required for custodial interrogation and he has been absconding since registration of the case.
He submits that if the petitioner is enlarged on anticipatory bail, he may not co-operate with the investigation and he may flee from justice.
9. It is no doubt true that the allegations are serious in nature.

However, the main allegations are against accused No.1 that he claiming to be in the administration of one Savitha Maharshi Degree College, issued bogus certificates to the foreign students to obtain services from FRRO, Bengaluru.

It is NC: 2023:KHC:21474 also alleged that accused No.2 is a working President of the college and he has permitted accused No.1 to prepare the letterheads etc. and he has also connived with the said accused.
As per the statement of CW.9, it was accused No.1 who has got printed the letterheads and got round seals prepared.
Petitioner is not named as an accused in the FIR.
It appears that on the basis of the voluntary statement of accused No.1, the petitioner is arraigned as an accused in this case.
The allegations are that, accused No.1 has given the letterheads and seals to the petitioner and he is a partner of accused No.1 hence, he is also involved in committing the offence.
The said allegations have to be established during trial.
Charge sheet is now filed showing the petitioner as accused No.3.
It is submitted that accused No.2 has been enlarged on bail by the learned Magistrate vide order dated 09.06.2023.
Petitioner has undertaken to co-operate with the investigation of the case and to regularly attend the Court proceedings.

Hence, the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

In the event of arrest of the petitioner/accused No.3 in Crime No.75/2023 of Sanjay Nagar Police Station, he shall be released subject to following conditions:
a) Petitioner shall appear before the learned Magistrate/jurisdictional Court within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of the order and shall execute a bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the said Court.
b) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of one week thereafter and shall co-operate with the further investigation of the case, if any.
c) Petitioner shall furnish his residential proof and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
